November 3, 2026 State Election Information 
 2026-11-03-Preliminary Results 
 The State Election will be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 . 
 READ THE CONSTABLES RETURN OF SERVICE FOR THE NOVEMBER 3, 2026 ELECTION WARRANT. 
 Lexington voters have the option to vote early by mail in all 2026 elections, with no excuse required.
 Forty-five days before each statewide election, the Secretary of the Commonwealth will send a pre-addressed, postage pre-paid Vote by Mail application to every registered voter before each statewide election. This mailing is required by state law .  
 You won’t be sent an application if you’ve already applied to vote by mail for the upcoming election.
 You can use this application to request a ballot for the next statewide election, or for all elections this year. Simply mark your selections, sign the application, and drop it in the mail. 
 The deadline  to request a ballot for November 3, 2026 State Election is Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 5:00 PM.

 On election day, polls will be open from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
 Important Deadlines:
 Voter Registration Deadline : You must be registered to vote by 5:00 PM on Saturday , October 24th, 2026 to participate in this election. You may register to vote online or in person at the Town Clerk's Office.  On Saturday, August 22nd, registration in person will be from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM in the Clerk's Office, 1625 Massachusetts Avenue.
 Mail-In Ballot Application  Deadline: If you wish to vote by mail, you must return a mail-in ballot application by 5:00 PM on Tuesday , October 27th, 2026 to vote by mail in this election.
 Excuse-required absentee voting by mail is available in all elections, to those who qualify. While early Vote by Mail ballots are more common, there are special circumstances where you may need to use the Absentee Ballot application to apply for an absentee ballot instead.
 Absentee Ballot Application  Deadline: You must apply to vote through an Absentee Ballot by 12:00 PM NOON on Monday , November 2, 2026. 
 You can vote by absentee ballot if: 
 You will be away from your city or town on Election Day
 You have a religious belief that prevents you from voting at your polling location on Election Day
 You have a disability that prevents you from voting at your polling location
